name: Orange Line elevated station (Dera Gujran as the mapped example)
assumptions: Rail level 12 m is the dossier's low-confidence figure; platform floor is set 1.05 m above it and all other levels stack from there.
Roof eaves 18 m and crown 21 m are fitted to one aerial construction photo and the platform photos, not measured.
Roof plan is the OSM ring rectified to a symmetric 29 m wide barrel with ends bowed 5 m; the ring's slight skew is ignored.
Platform and deck use the published 102 x 22.5 m; the roof overhangs them to fill the 109 x 29 m ring, and the ring may include that overhang.
Photos used are of the Chauburji station and an unnamed station under construction; Dera Gujran is assumed to share the standard design.
Concourse drum length (76 m), its belly profile and the ribbon window height come from the dossier's description only; the exterior photo of it could not be fetched.
Footbridge position at mid-station, their length, and the stair layout are plain guesses from the dossier's 'footbridges either side'.
Column layout under the station (two rows of round piers) is assumed; single T-head piers are photographed on the approaches only.
Viaduct is cut at a pier on each side as a short stub; the real line continues.
Rib spacing 8.4 m and X bracing in alternate bays are estimated from platform photos; bay count may be off by one or two.
Intermediate raked columns are pale (Chauburji photo) and end columns orange (aerial photo); colours may vary by station.
Platform rooms: four, positions and sizes estimated from the Chauburji platform. Stair and escalator openings in the platforms are left out.
Screen doors appear at Chauburji in photos; the dossier notes Wikipedia confirms them only underground.
A five-car train is parked at one platform as dressing to show the documented livery; set SHOW_TRAIN False to remove it. Car length 19 m is an estimate.
Colours other than the dossier's soffit hex are photo estimates.
